title: Clean up deployment records left in the file system
description:
https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/pull/844 introduced a breaking change to the CLI, in which if there is a deployment record on disk, it will try to deploy to that same location, regardless of what the default server/credentials are. That breaks workflows using `connect-actions` that deploy to multiple Connect servers, because even though we log out and log in to the new server, the deployment record is still on disk.

Regardless of whether the CLI behavior change is a good idea, we can prevent this by cleaning up any deployment records when we tear down from the action, just as we log out. That seems like a good practice anyway.

title: Document and add to skill for GitHub OIDC changes
description:
See https://github.blog/changelog/2026-04-23-immutable-subject-claims-for-github-actions-oidc-tokens/

Repos created on/after 2026-07-15 use immutable subject claims by default (older repos can opt in). 

The `gh` invocation to retrieve this is:

```bash
# From within a local clone of the repository:
gh api "repos/$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner)" \
  --jq '"\(.owner.login)@\(.owner.id)/\(.name)@\(.id)"'

# Or, for any repository by name:
gh api "repos/$ORG/$REPO" \
  --jq '"\(.owner.login)@\(.owner.id)/\(.name)@\(.id)"'
```

We should document this in the readme, and in the skill, offer to help set up trusted publishing on the repo. Use `posit-cli`, it can `posit connect login <server_url>` and then use `posit connect api ...` to set the trusted publishing repo, derived using `gh` from the current repo as noted above. https://docs.posit.co/connect/api/#post-/v1/content/-guid-/trusted-publishers describes the POST request needed to set it up.

title: README: Trusted Publishing is configured on the Source tab, not Access

> You can enable this in the "Access" tab of the content settings.

In the upcoming version of Connect the "Trusted Publishing" section will be under the "Source" tab alongside the active bundle and runtime versions.

The skill says "Source" already, but the `README` still says "Access". We should change it with the next release of Connect.

title: Refactor logic around requirements generation
description:
#75 adds another condition to govern whether to (re)generate a requirements.txt from a uv.lock or pyproject.toml, based on app modes. This mostly works but would break down for R content that uses reticulate, and in general feels like we're making extra complicated logic with functions that have many arguments switching off behavior.

I wonder if there's a cleaner way we can solve this. As in, if the working directory contains a pyproject.toml or uv.lock but no requirements.txt, run the generate-requirements step. (I'm not sure what this would do for python content that contains no requirements files of any kind, we might need to confirm that it errors cleanly.)

title: Deploy fails for most app modes: app_mode → deploy subcommand mapping is incomplete
description:
`resolve_app_type` maps a Connect `app_mode` to a `posit connect deploy` subcommand, but most `app_mode` names don't match.

    $ posit connect deploy python-gradio
    Error: No such command 'python-gradio'. Did you mean 'gradio'?

The authoritative app_mode list is `AppModeFromString` in
`src/connect/worker/apptypes/apptypes.go:82`, not the [manifest docs
page][docs].

Deploy subcommands come from `AppModes._cli_aliases` in `rsconnect-python`.

## Works today

| app_mode           | subcommand                                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `python-shiny`     | `shiny`                                           |
| `python-fastapi`   | `fastapi`                                         |
| `python-dash`      | `dash`                                            |
| `python-streamlit` | `streamlit`                                       |
| `python-bokeh`     | `bokeh`                                           |
| `quarto-static`    | `quarto`                                          |
| `nodejs`           | `nodejs` — by accident; the names happen to match |

## Broken: the subcommand exists, we don't map it

| app_mode                  | subcommand         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `python-api` (Flask/WSGI) | `api` (or `flask`) |
| `python-gradio`           | `gradio`           |
| `python-panel`            | `panel`            |
| `jupyter-static`          | `notebook`         |
| `jupyter-voila`           | `voila`            |
| `tensorflow-saved-model`  | `tensorflow`       |
| `static`                  | `html`             |

## No correct subcommand to map to

- `shiny`, `rmd-shiny`, `rmd-static`, `api` — R content; these already error
  today asking for a `manifest.json`
- `quarto-shiny` — silently deploys as `quarto-static` via `posit connect
  deploy quarto`; needs `... deploy manifest` instead
- `proxied` — no CLI alias at all; not deployable from source

`shiny` and `api` are the sharp edge here: subcommands by those names do
exist, but they mean `python-shiny` and `python-api` (see below), so mapping
them straight through would deploy R content as Python.

## Also

`APP_MODE_TO_TYPE` contains a `python-flask` key, but no such app_mode
exists — Connect reports Flask content as `python-api`. That entry never
fires, and Flask content fails.

`api` and `shiny` mean different things in the two namespaces: as app_modes
they are R Plumber and R Shiny, as CLI aliases they are `python-api` and
`python-shiny`.

## Proposed fix

Fill in the missing modes, delete the dead `python-flask` key, and route
`quarto-shiny` and `proxied` to explicit errors.

Replace the fall-through with a clear error naming the supported modes, since
passing an unmapped mode through provably produces `No such command`.
Parametrize the tests over all 20 modes in `AppModeFromString` so a mode Connect
adds later fails loudly instead of falling through.

## Docs discrepancy (separate, connect repo)

The [manifest docs page][docs] lists `jupyter` and `quarto`, which
`AppModeFromString` rejects, and omits `rmd-shiny`, `nodejs`, and `proxied`.
Worth a docs issue; not in scope here.

Found while reviewing #75 — see [Neal's comment][comment].

[docs]: https://docs.posit.co/connect/user/manifest/index.html#appmode
[comment]: https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-actions/pull/75#discussion_r3721015531

title: Deploying Node.js content fails at the requirements-generation step
description:
The deploy action's "Generate requirements.txt if needed" step runs for every app type and exits 1 unless the app directory has a `manifest.json`, `requirements.txt`, `uv.lock`, or `pyproject.toml`. Node.js content legitimately has none of these (its dependencies come from `package.json`/`package-lock.json`), so a manifest-free nodejs deploy fails with "No uv.lock or pyproject.toml file found" even though `posit connect deploy nodejs` handles it fine.

The app type is already resolved before the step runs, so the fix is to skip requirements generation for content without Python dependencies.

title: `rsconnect-args` can't pass argument values containing spaces
description:
[`deploy/scripts/deploy.sh`](https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-actions/blob/44ddd9dfe2c3101994145e038101711eaf0f8f8a/deploy/scripts/deploy.sh#L103) expands the input unquoted:

```bash
posit connect deploy "$APP_TYPE" ... ${RSCONNECT_ARGS:-} "$DEPLOY_TARGET" ...
```

Plain word-splitting with no quote parsing means `rsconnect-args: --title "My App"` reaches the CLI as three tokens — `--title`, `"My` (literal quote included), `App"` — and fails with `Got unexpected extra argument`. There is no way to express a value containing whitespace.

This matters in practice: until posit-dev/rsconnect-python#835 is fixed, passing `--title` matching the content's exact title is the only way to deploy a manifest under trusted publishing — and content titles routinely contain spaces.

**Suggested fix:** parse `RSCONNECT_ARGS` with shell quoting rules (e.g. Python `shlex.split` in the existing `connect_actions` package, emitting a newline-delimited list like `EXTRA_FILES` already uses), and/or add a dedicated `title:` input that's passed as a properly quoted single argument.

title: setup-connect-deploy skill: Trusted Publishing config has moved from the Access tab to the Source tab
description:
The `setup-connect-deploy` skill (`skills/setup-connect-deploy/SKILL.md`) tells users to configure a trusted publisher for their content on the content's **Access** tab in Connect, in two places:

- Step 3, Option A: "a trusted publisher configured for this content (on the content's **Access** tab in Connect, tied to this GitHub repo)"
- Step 7 wrap-up: "**OIDC:** enable Trusted Publishing for this content on Connect (Access tab), tied to this GitHub repo"

In current Connect, this setting lives on the **Source** tab, not the Access tab. Users following the skill's instructions verbatim will look in the wrong place after their OIDC deploy fails with "Connect did not grant access for this identity token."

Observed on Connect at 2026-08-04 while setting up posit-dev/commons with the deploy action.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Better error when no manifest.json: don't assume Python content
description:
## What happened

Deploying an R project (with `renv.lock`) without a `manifest.json`, the deploy step ran `generate-requirements.sh` and failed with a Python-specific error:

```
No uv.lock or pyproject.toml file found. Please run 'uv sync' to generate uv.lock or create a pyproject.toml before deploying.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The action appears to assume Python content whenever `manifest.json` is absent. For an R project this error is confusing and misleading — it points the user toward `uv`/`pyproject.toml` when the actual requirement is an R manifest.

## Expected behavior

- Don't assume Python content solely because `manifest.json` is missing.
- Detect content type (e.g. presence of `renv.lock`, `.R`/`.Rmd`/`.qmd` files, `DESCRIPTION`, etc.) before choosing the requirements-generation path.
- Produce an error message tailored to the detected content type. For R content, the message should explain that a `manifest.json` is required (and how to generate one) rather than mentioning `uv.lock`/`pyproject.toml`.

title: Investigate Quarto installation needs for `quarto-shiny` app mode
description:
## Context

In #64, we added Quarto installation support for `quarto-static` content (the `quarto` deploy subcommand requires `quarto inspect` locally). The `quarto-shiny` app mode currently maps to the `shiny` deploy subcommand, so we don't install Quarto for it.

However, it's unclear whether `rsconnect-python` (via `posit connect deploy shiny`) needs a local Quarto installation to render/inspect the `.qmd` before deploying a `quarto-shiny` app, or whether Connect handles that entirely server-side.

## Questions to answer

- Does `posit connect deploy shiny` for a `quarto-shiny` app require a local Quarto installation (e.g., for `quarto inspect` or rendering)?
- If so, should we install Quarto when the `app_mode` is `quarto-shiny` in addition to `quarto-static`?

## Current behavior

In `src/connect_actions/apptype.py`, `quarto-shiny` maps to deploy type `shiny` with `needs_quarto=False`:

```python
APP_MODE_TO_TYPE: dict[str, str] = {
    ...
    "quarto-static": "quarto",
    "quarto-shiny": "shiny",
}
```

## Action items

- [ ] Test deploying a `quarto-shiny` app through the deploy action without Quarto installed locally
- [ ] If it fails, update `resolve_app_type()` to set `needs_quarto=True` for `quarto-shiny`
- [ ] Add an e2e test for `quarto-shiny` if support is needed

## References

- PR #64 (Install quarto if needed)
- [Review discussion](https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-actions/pull/64#discussion_r3604428476)

title: Test config resolution from a deployment TOML file
description:
Follow-up to #3 (e2e tests added in #31). The e2e job currently only exercises `resolve-config.sh` **tier 1** (explicit `connect-server` + `content-guid` inputs). The TOML-based resolution paths are untested:

- **Tier 2** — `deployment-file` input pointing at a specific `.posit` TOML.
- **Tier 3** — auto-detection of a single `.toml` in `.posit/publish/deployments/`, plus the error cases (no directory, zero files, multiple files, missing file).
- **`parse-deployment-toml.py`** — both the `deploy` and `cleanup-previews` copies (the deploy one also extracts `entrypoint`).

This is the "commit the Posit Publisher TOML and let the action pick everything up" workflow, which is a headline feature in the README, so it's worth real coverage — especially before/while consolidating the near-duplicate `resolve-config.sh` / `parse-deployment-toml.py` between the two actions.

### Sketch

The content GUID is created at runtime, so the TOML can't be fully checked in. Write a `.posit/publish/deployments/*.toml` at test time containing the created server + GUID (+ `entrypoint`), then invoke `deploy` with **no** explicit `connect-server`/`content-guid` and assert it resolves and deploys. A second case can point `deployment-file` at a TOML in a non-default location.

Error cases (zero/multiple TOMLs) can be asserted by running just the resolve step and checking it exits non-zero with the expected message.

title: Rewrite Bash helper scripts as a unit-tested Python package
description:
## Summary

Rewrite the Bash helper scripts in the composite actions as a single, unit-tested Python package. Python is already guaranteed on the runner (we install `uv` and already use Python for TOML parsing), so we can consolidate the shell logic into testable functions and `import` `rsconnect-python` where it helps.

This is motivated by the fact that the script logic (config resolution, `app_mode` → subcommand mapping, metadata-arg building, deployment-file auto-detection) is pure logic that is painful to test in Bash and currently has **no tests at all**.

## Scope

The four `.sh` files plus the two already-Python TOML parsers:

| File | Lines | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `deploy/scripts/deploy.sh` | 100 | `app_mode` lookup (curl+jq), metadata-arg building, `rsconnect deploy`, URL scraping |
| `deploy/scripts/resolve-config.sh` | 51 | 3-tier config resolution, TOML auto-detect |
| `cleanup-previews/scripts/resolve-config.sh` | 50 | near-duplicate of the above |
| `deploy/scripts/generate-requirements.sh` | 26 | `uv pip compile` |
| `deploy/scripts/parse-deployment-toml.py` | 20 | already Python (near-duplicate) |
| `cleanup-previews/scripts/parse-deployment-toml.py` | 16 | already Python (near-duplicate) |

**Out of scope (for now):**
- `get-api-key/get-api-key.sh` — OIDC exchange has moved into rsconnect-python (posit-dev/rsconnect-python#802). There is likely a larger change to make here (`rsconnect login` shared across action steps); tracked separately.
- The inline `actions/github-script` JavaScript in both `action.yml` files (PR comment / bundle-ID logic) — that's JS tied to the github-script action; leave as-is.

## Target layout

A real package at the repo root (not PEP 723 single-files), so shared code and `pytest` are clean:

```
connect-actions/
  pyproject.toml                 # package "connect_actions", python>=3.11, dev dep: pytest
  src/connect_actions/
    __init__.py
    config.py                    # resolve_config() — pure logic
    cli.py                       # argparse dispatch + GITHUB_OUTPUT writing (thin I/O shell)
    requirements.py              # generate-requirements
    deploy.py                    # app_mode lookup, metadata args, deploy
  tests/
    test_config.py
  deploy/action.yml              # step: uv run --project ${{ github.action_path }}/.. python -m connect_actions.cli resolve-config
  cleanup-previews/action.yml    # same module, ignores entrypoint
```

Both actions already reach sibling code via `${{ github.action_path }}/../…` (that's how `get-api-key` is invoked), so `--project ${{ github.action_path }}/..` points `uv` at the repo-root `pyproject.toml` while `working-directory: ${{ inputs.path }}` keeps the user's app dir as cwd.

## Design principles

- **Pure functions + thin `main()`.** All logic in importable functions with typed inputs/outputs; a thin CLI layer reads env, writes `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, and shells out. Only the thin layer touches I/O.
- **Collapse the duplication.** The two `resolve-config.sh` + two `parse-deployment-toml.py` become one `config.py`; deploy needs the extra `entrypoint` field, cleanup just ignores it.
- **Drop the `toml` dependency** in favor of stdlib `tomllib` (pin python>=3.11 via `uv`).
- **Keep the `action.yml` env-var contract identical** so the rewrite is mechanical from the actions' perspective.
- **Add CI** — there is no test/lint CI today. Add a workflow that runs `uv run pytest`.

## One real design decision: `rsconnect deploy`

The deploy itself stays a side-effecting invocation. Two options:
1. **Subprocess the CLI** and parse stdout for the content URL (what `deploy.sh` does today via grep+sed). Smallest change.
2. **Use `rsconnect-python` as a library** and get the URL back as structured data — no log-scraping, more testable, but couples to rsconnect internals.

Start with (1) to keep the rewrite mechanical; revisit (2) later, likely alongside the `rsconnect login` / shared-session work.

## Suggested order (incremental PRs)

1. **Config resolution** (`resolve-config.sh` + `parse-deployment-toml.py`, both actions → `config.py` + tests). Self-contained, already half-Python, most duplicated, pure logic. Establishes the `pyproject.toml` / `src` layout, the `pytest` harness, the CI workflow, and the `uv run` invocation pattern that everything else reuses.
2. **`generate-requirements.sh`** → `requirements.py`.
3. **`deploy.sh`** → `deploy.py` (the big one; carries the CLI-vs-library decision above).

## First bite: config resolution

Behavior must match the current 3-tier resolution: (1) explicit `connect-server`+`content-guid` inputs, (2) specified `deployment-file`, (3) auto-detect exactly one `.toml` under `.posit/publish/deployments/` (current Bash uses recursive `find`, so use `rglob`). Error messages preserved for: missing dir, zero files, multiple files, missing specified file.

Tests cover: explicit inputs win; single-toml auto-detect (incl. `entrypoint`); multiple-toml error; missing-dir error.

title: Run e2e tests across a matrix of Connect versions
description:
Follow-up to #3 (e2e tests added in #31). The e2e job pins a single Connect version (`2025.12.0`, the minimum that supports the `--metadata` bundle-upload API — see #736). We should run the suite against a matrix of Connect versions so we catch version-specific regressions and verify the action's supported range.

### Why

- The action interacts with Connect APIs (`app_mode` lookup, bundle upload with metadata, bundles list/delete) whose behavior varies by version.
- We already hit two version-sensitive issues while building the test: the metadata upload requires Connect ≥ 2025.12.0, and Connect matches the manifest's Python version exactly (we now query `server_settings/python` to pick a valid one).
- A matrix documents and enforces the minimum supported version, and surfaces breakage on newer/`release` builds early.

### Sketch

`strategy.matrix.connect-version: [<min supported>, ..., release]` feeding `with-connect`'s `version` input, `fail-fast: false`. Note the interaction with metadata: versions older than 2025.12.0 will fail until the action degrades gracefully (#34), so the matrix floor depends on that work — or the older-version legs assert the expected graceful behavior instead.

Watch CI cost: each leg pulls a Connect image and runs a full deploy, so keep the matrix small (e.g. min, a mid version, `release`).

title: Don't send bundle metadata on Connect versions that don't support it
description:
Discovered while building the e2e tests (#3 / #31).

The `deploy` action **always** passes `--metadata` to `rsconnect deploy` (added in #15). That routes through rsconnect's multipart bundle-upload API, which requires **Connect ≥ 2025.12.0** ([rsconnect-python #736](https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/pull/736)). `rsconnect` detects the Connect version and uses that to decide whether to sniff the git checkout for metadata, but if you explicitly send `--metadata`, it assumes you know what you're doing and does it, and fails if it doesn't work. 

Net effect: **the action silently requires Connect ≥ 2025.12.0** today. (This is why the e2e test pins `2025.12.0`.)

### What to do

1. **Detect Connect's capability/version and skip `--metadata` when unsupported.** e.g. read the server version and only add metadata args when the server supports the metadata upload API. This makes the action work on older Connect again (without the rich provenance metadata).
2. Document the minimum Connect version for full functionality in the README as well as how it degrades.

Relates to #33 (the version matrix can't include older Connect until this is handled, or it must assert the graceful behavior).

title: Translate uv.lock to requirements.txt

title: Make PR previews work with multiple servers
description:
So that you can (1) deploy previews to multiple environments and (2) if using OIDC, be able to have cleanup work without arguments.

In cleanup, we can pick up the Connect server URL from the comment, so we don't need to take it as an argument. Alternatively, if you're using API keys, and there are more than one preview comments, you need to specify more than one cleanup step, one for each key, and indicating the Connect server (i.e. you need server and API key as a pair). If there is only one comment then you don't need to provide the server, it can be inferred from the comment.

For leaving the comment, when we look to update the comment, we need to be sure we're finding the one with the content URL in it so that we update the correct comment.

title: Support deploying with a manifest.json

But until we can support #2 and other things, and for compatibility with existing workflows we've promoted, it should be possible to deploy with a manifest.json you have checked in.

title: Provide better git metadata
description: All of this would be by passing extra `--metadata key=value` args to `rsconnect` CLI. * The SHA shows up as "dirty" because we've done a uv install and have generated the requirements.txt. Always pass the SHA as `source_commit` * The branch ref shows up as `HEAD` on pull requests. This looks to be because things run in the merge with the target branch ([example](https://github.com/posit-dev/zendesk-mcp-server/commit/cf0ce4b06423e637755ec7051a2f4fe21e402b99)), not on the branch itself (the difference between `pull_request` and `pull_request_target` triggers). Get the PR branch name and pass that `source_branch` * Set the `source` to be "github-actions" so we can distinguish bundles that came from here. * Include more stuff: * on PR, include the PR title, on commit to main, the commit message one-liner. Let's call that `source_description` * the URL to the run. Let's call that `source_github_actions_run` * on PR, include PR number as `source_pull_request` * send the commit author's github username as `source_author`

title: Do OIDC token exchange
description:
Claude says it looks something like this: 

```
        # 1. Get the OIDC token from GitHub
        - name: Get OIDC token
          uses: actions/github-script@v7
          id: oidc
          with:
            script: |
              const token = await core.getIDToken('posit-connect');
              core.setOutput('token', token);

        # 2. Exchange it for a Connect API key
        - name: Exchange token for Connect API key
          id: connect-token
          run: |
            RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST \
              "${{ vars.CONNECT_URL }}/v1/oauth/credentials/" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
              -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" \
              -d "subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token" \
              -d "subject_token=${{ steps.oidc.outputs.token }}" \
              -d "requested_token_type=urn:posit:connect:api-key")

            API_KEY=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.access_token')

            if [ "$API_KEY" = "null" ] || [ -z "$API_KEY" ]; then
              echo "Token exchange failed:"
              echo "$RESPONSE" | jq .
              exit 1
            fi

            echo "::add-mask::$API_KEY"
            echo "api_key=$API_KEY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

Instead of using `'posit-connect'` as the ID Token audience, use the connect server URL, stripped of protocol and trailing slash (e.g. `connect.posit.it`). 

Do this whenever the connect-api-key parameter is not set. Fail with a clear message: ideally disambiguating bad request with a misconfiguration from the case where the OIDC federation integration has not been set up, or where the version of Connect in question does not have the feature. But when in doubt, say API key is required.

title: Notes on dependency and lockfile management
description:
Don't want to require double bookkeeping everywhere, especially with manifest.json since it is Connect-only and requires Connect tooling to generate. But:

* If repositories are private, GitHub Actions can't generate the right lockfile from pyproject.toml or R files, unless the repos are set there. ([If PPM, they have OIDC support.](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/integrations/openid-connect-identity-federation.html#github-actions-integration)) This is a problem unless/until Connect can support installing from pyproject.toml etc. without a requirements.txt
* Python: There was some issue using uv to turn uv.lock into requirements.txt (todo write an issue)

In R, 
* `rsconnect::writeManifest()` can take a renv.lock, but it [requires packages to be installed](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/931), which may not always be possible.
* `renv::renv_lockfile_from_manifest()` exists to go manifest to renv.lock, but not the other way.
* Publisher has typescript code to [convert renv.lock to manifest.json](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/7d89d1b9443350f67b1d5a51ae0241a83df982f6/extensions/vscode/src/publish/rPackageDescriptions.ts)
* There is also a `pak` lockfile? https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/lockfile_create.html

For all languages:

* If a manifest.json exists, use it. Assume user knows about it and updates it out of band. (#16)
* Else, if a lockfile exists (uv.lock, renv.lock, others), use it. Assume that user is managing the lockfile on their own (pre-commit hook, other workflow, etc.) (#22)
* Else, if a project requirements file exists (pyproject.toml, DESCRIPTION, etc.), the action should generate a lockfile with it and use that. Assumption is that private packages or repos are either not used by the project or are configured in the workflow. (needs issue to pick up DESCRIPTION file)

title: New action: render a document on Connect
description: Maybe you have a workflow that updates a pin on Connect, or maybe it updates data in some other system (or, maybe you're doing something with data in GitHub), and you have a document that you want to re-render with the latest data. We could provide an Action that fires off that API request.
